text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: Sega Hikaru was a high-end arcade hardware platform released by Sega in 1999. Based on technology related to the Sega Dreamcast's Naomi architecture, Hikaru used a custom graphics system designed for advanced real-time 3D rendering with effects such as particle systems, lighting, and transparency. The hardware was created for visually impressive arcade experiences and powered games including Brave Firefighters, Star Wars Racer Arcade, Planet Harriers, and Sega Marine Fishing. Due to its high manufacturing cost and limited number of compatible games, Hikaru was produced in small quantities and remains one of Sega's rarest arcade platforms.
